work: Chemistry bridges the physical sciences (physics, mathematics) and the life/earth sciences (biology, geology, medicine), which is why it is called the central science. The other options restrict chemistry falsely.
cleanExplanation: Chemistry is called the central science because its principles connect physics and mathematics with biology, geology and medicine. It is not limited to laboratory work, is not the oldest science, and certainly does not study only living things.

work: The Haber process combines atmospheric N2 with H2 over an iron catalyst to make NH3, the feedstock for nitrogen fertilizers. The other options are unrelated industrial processes.
cleanExplanation: The Haber process fixes nitrogen from the air by reacting N<sub>2</sub> with H<sub>2</sub> over an iron catalyst to produce ammonia, which is the basis of nitrogen fertilizers. work: Chemistry is defined as the study of matter, its properties, and the changes it undergoes. It does relate to environmental issues, does make predictions, and studies natural as well as synthetic materials.
cleanExplanation: Chemistry is the study of matter, its properties and the changes it undergoes. It is closely tied to environmental issues, is strongly predictive, and covers both natural and man-made substances.

work: CFCs release chlorine radicals in the stratosphere that catalytically destroy ozone, so they were banned under the Montreal Protocol. They are not radioactive, are not an acid-rain source, and are not explosive.
cleanExplanation: CFCs rise to the stratosphere, where ultraviolet light breaks them apart and the released chlorine atoms catalytically destroy ozone molecules. This depletion of the ozone layer, which shields Earth from UV radiation, is why they were phased out.

work: Green chemistry aims to design processes and products that reduce or eliminate hazardous substances and waste. It does not ban reactions, ignore cost for speed, or require only natural products.
cleanExplanation: A central goal of green chemistry is designing chemical processes and products that reduce or eliminate hazardous waste and the use and generation of dangerous substances. It does not mean avoiding reactions, maximizing speed regardless of cost, or using only natural products.

work: The macroscopic domain covers properties and changes observable and measurable directly on bulk samples, as opposed to the microscopic (atomic/molecular) and symbolic levels.
cleanExplanation: The macroscopic level refers to what can be observed and measured directly, such as mass, color, temperature and volume of a bulk sample. Atoms, molecules and nuclei belong to the microscopic (particulate) level.

work: A solution turning blue is a directly observable property of the bulk sample. Atom rearrangement, electron transitions and bond breaking are particulate-level events.
cleanExplanation: A solution turning blue is something you can see and measure directly on the bulk sample, so it is a macroscopic observation. Atoms rearranging, electrons moving between orbitals and bonds breaking all describe the microscopic, particulate level.

work: Explaining a bulk property (ice floating, i.e. lower density) by how water molecules are arranged and hydrogen bonded is a particulate-level explanation.
cleanExplanation: Explaining why ice floats requires describing how H<sub>2</sub>O molecules pack into an open hydrogen-bonded lattice that is less dense than liquid water. That is an explanation at the microscopic (particle) level, used to account for a macroscopic observation.

work: The statement that mass is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction is the law of conservation of mass. The other laws concern fixed mass ratios and gas volume ratios.
cleanExplanation: The law of conservation of mass states that mass is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction, so the total mass of reactants equals that of products. The laws of definite and multiple proportions and of combining volumes describe fixed mass or volume ratios instead.

work: A substance is a form of matter with a fixed, definite composition and distinct properties (an element or a compound), unlike a mixture. Being a solid or being natural is irrelevant.
cleanExplanation: A substance is matter with a fixed composition and distinct properties, such as an element or a compound. Mixtures have variable composition, and a substance need not be a solid or a natural material.
